As a professional frontend developer, a few thoughts on this:

  • Google seems a bit overly aggressive in writing YouTube in Polymer. Polymer is an idea they've stuck with for a few years and continue to push, so they probably wanted to show how it can perform and scale in the real world. The downside is that native browser support just hasn't caught up yet.
  • Polymer has been on Shadow DOM v1 since version 2. Mozilla is complaining that YouTube is using Shadow DOM v0, meaning they would have to be on Polymer 1. Are you telling me they are two full versions behind on their own product? Something seems wrong here.
  • The performance issues should go away in Firefox if you enable the dom.webcomponents.shadowdom.enabled flag. What is preventing Mozilla from making this a default feature?
  • Edge is consistently the farthest behind in implementing new standards. I don't feel bad for them.

Ultimately it's Google being Google and other browser developers being lazy. Google has done a great deal to move web standards forward. Occasionally they go too far (like with AMP), but I don't see it here. If Google really is still on Polymer 1, then it's only a matter of time until this sorts itself out. If they are on Polymer 2 or 3, the browser vendors shouldn't be complaining if they themselves just haven't caught up with new standards yet.
